notes:
Displacement Current

  • Maxwell added displacement current $I_d = \varepsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ to Ampere's law to make it consistent with charge conservation (e.g. inside a charging capacitor, where conduction current is zero but $E$ is changing).
  • Modified Ampere–Maxwell law: $\oint \vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0(I_c + I_d)$.

Nature of EM Waves

  • Accelerated charges radiate EM waves. $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ oscillate perpendicular to each other and to the direction of propagation (transverse), in phase, with $\dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = c$.
  • Speed in vacuum $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}} = 3\times10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$; in a medium $v = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}}$, refractive index $n = \sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}$.
  • EM waves carry energy and momentum; they exert radiation pressure. For total absorption $p = U/c$; for total reflection $p = 2U/c$.
  • EM waves do not need a medium and are unaffected by electric/magnetic fields (they are neutral).

Electromagnetic Spectrum

RadiationWavelength rangeProductionUse
Radio>0.1 mOscillating circuitsCommunication
Microwave0.1 m–1 mmKlystron/magnetronRadar, ovens
Infrared1 mm–700 nmHot bodiesNight vision, remotes
Visible700–400 nmAtomic transitionsVision
Ultraviolet400–1 nmSun, arc lampsSterilisation
X-rays1 nm–$10^{-3}$ nmSudden deceleration of electronsMedical imaging
Gamma rays<$10^{-3}$ nmNuclear decayCancer treatment
  • Increasing frequency order: radio < microwave < IR < visible < UV < X-ray < gamma. The ozone layer absorbs harmful UV; greenhouse effect is due to IR trapping by CO$_2$/water vapour.

    • Exam tip

    KCET usually asks 1 question, almost always on the electromagnetic spectrum order/uses or the direction/ratio of $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and $\vec{k}$. Memorise the spectrum table and the displacement current formula.

questions.q: Displacement current arises due to
options: motion of free electrons in a conductor
questions.explanation: Maxwell defined $I_d = \varepsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$, which exists wherever the electric flux through a surface changes with time, such as between capacitor plates while charging.

questions.q: In an electromagnetic wave travelling along the $+x$ direction, the electric field is along $y$. The magnetic field is along
questions.explanation: $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ and the direction of propagation $\vec{k}$ are mutually perpendicular, forming a right-handed set; $\hat{y}\times\hat{z} = \hat{x}$, so $\vec{B}$ is along $z$.

questions.q: The ratio of amplitudes of electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave in vacuum equals
questions.explanation: $E_0/B_0 = c$, the speed of light, a direct consequence of Maxwell's equations.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with circular plates of radius 5 cm is being charged. At an instant, the conduction current is 2 A. The displacement current between the plates at that instant is
questions.explanation: In series with the charging circuit, the displacement current between the plates always equals the conduction current in the wires, so $I_d = 2$ A.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly orders the electromagnetic spectrum by increasing frequency?
options: Visible, UV, IR, X-rays, gamma rays, radio, microwave
Radio, microwave, IR, visible, UV, X-rays, gamma rays
Microwave, radio, IR, visible, UV, gamma rays, X-rays
Gamma rays, X-rays, UV, visible, IR, microwave, radio
questions.explanation: Frequency increases as radio < microwave < infrared < visible < ultraviolet < X-rays < gamma rays (wavelength decreases in the same order).

questions.q: X-rays are produced by
options: sudden deceleration of fast-moving electrons on striking a metal target
vibration of atoms in a hot filament
questions.explanation: In an X-ray tube, high-energy electrons are suddenly stopped by a metal (target) anode; the lost kinetic energy is emitted as X-ray photons (bremsstrahlung).

questions.q: The layer of the atmosphere that absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun is the
questions.explanation: Ozone (O$_3$) in the stratosphere absorbs UV radiation, protecting living organisms from its harmful effects.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of intensity $I$ falls normally on a perfectly reflecting surface of area $A$ and is completely reflected. The radiation pressure exerted is
questions.explanation: For total reflection, momentum transferred per unit area per unit time is $2I/c$ (energy $U=I$ per unit area per unit time, and $p = 2U/c$ for reflection).

questions.q: The refractive index of a non-magnetic ($\mu_r \approx 1$) medium with relative permittivity 2.25 for electromagnetic waves is
questions.explanation: $n = \sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r} = \sqrt{1\times2.25} = 1.5$.

questions.q: Which statement about electromagnetic waves is correct?
options: They are transverse waves in which $E$ and $B$ oscillate in phase
They are deflected by electric and magnetic fields since they consist of $E$ and $B$
They carry energy but not momentum
They require a material medium to propagate
questions.explanation: EM waves are transverse, need no medium, are electrically neutral (not deflected by fields), and carry both energy and momentum; $E$ and $B$ oscillate in phase.

questions.q: Microwaves are best suited for radar systems because they
options: travel slower than light, giving more accurate ranging
are absorbed strongly by metal objects
have short wavelength and can be transmitted as narrow beams
have very low frequency and diffract around obstacles
questions.explanation: Microwaves have short wavelength, allowing them to be formed into narrow directional beams (using small antennas) that reflect off targets, ideal for radar.

questions.q: In an electromagnetic wave, the energy density stored in the electric field, on time-averaging, is
options: much greater than that in the magnetic field
equal to that in the magnetic field
much less than that in the magnetic field
questions.explanation: For an EM wave, average electric energy density $\dfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_{rms}^2$ equals average magnetic energy density $\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{B_{rms}^2}{\mu_0}$, each contributing equally to total energy.

questions.q: Infrared radiation is often called heat radiation mainly because
options: it is emitted only by radioactive substances
it has the highest frequency in the EM spectrum
it travels faster than visible light
it is strongly absorbed by water molecules in the skin producing a heating effect
questions.explanation: Infrared photons are readily absorbed by water and other molecules, increasing their kinetic energy (heat), which is why IR lamps are used for warming.

questions.q: If the amplitude of the magnetic field in an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is $2\times10^{-7}$ T, the amplitude of the electric field is (take $c = 3\times10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: $E_0 = cB_0 = 3\times10^8\times2\times10^{-7} = 60$ V/m.

questions.q: The wave equation of Maxwell's theory shows that the speed of light in vacuum is
questions.explanation: $c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}}$, so $c$ is inversely proportional to $\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}$.

questions.q: Gamma rays used in the treatment of cancer are produced by
options: de-excitation of nuclei following radioactive decay
sudden stopping of electrons in an X-ray tube
questions.explanation: Gamma rays originate from nuclear transitions/decays, unlike X-rays which arise from electron transitions or deceleration; this is a common point of confusion in KCET.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave has frequency $6\times10^{14}$ Hz. Its wavelength in vacuum is closest to
questions.explanation: $\lambda = c/f = \dfrac{3\times10^8}{6\times10^{14}} = 5\times10^{-7}\ \text{m} = 500$ nm, in the visible (green) range.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a property of electromagnetic waves?
options: They travel with the same speed $c$ in vacuum regardless of frequency
They show reflection, refraction, interference and diffraction
They obey the principle of superposition
questions.explanation: EM waves are transverse, not longitudinal; all the other listed properties (superposition, constant vacuum speed, wave phenomena) are correct.

questions.q: The direction of energy flow (and wave propagation) in an electromagnetic wave is given by the direction of
options: the Poynting vector, $\vec S = \vec E \times \vec H$
questions.explanation: The Poynting vector $\vec S=\vec E\times\vec H$ gives both the direction and magnitude of energy flux carried by an electromagnetic wave, and points along the direction of propagation.

questions.q: The peak electric field of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is 100 V/m. The average intensity of the wave is (use $I=\frac12\varepsilon_0cE_0^2$, $\varepsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}$ C$^2$/N m$^2$)
questions.explanation: $I=\dfrac12\times8.85\times10^{-12}\times3\times10^8\times(100)^2\approx13.3$ W/m$^2$.

questions.q: The total average energy density of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum, in terms of the rms electric field $E_{rms}$, is
questions.explanation: Electric and magnetic energy densities are equal, each averaging $\frac12\varepsilon_0E_{rms}^2$; their sum gives total average energy density $u=\varepsilon_0E_{rms}^2$.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave has wavelength 500 nm in vacuum. Its wave number $k=2\pi/\lambda$ is
questions.explanation: $k=2\pi/\lambda=2\pi/(5\times10^{-7})\approx1.26\times10^{7}$ m$^{-1}$.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave travels along the $-y$ direction with its electric field along $+z$. The magnetic field must be along
questions.explanation: Propagation direction is along $\vec E\times\vec B$; with $\vec E$ along $+z$ and propagation along $-y$, $\vec B$ must be along $-x$, since $\hat z\times(-\hat x)=-\hat y$.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of field amplitudes ($E_0$, $B_0$) is consistent with a valid electromagnetic wave travelling in vacuum?
questions.explanation: A valid EM wave in vacuum requires $E_0/B_0=c=3\times10^8$ m/s; only $300/(1\times10^{-6})=3\times10^8$ satisfies this.

questions.q: A radio wave has a wavelength of 300 m. Its frequency is
questions.explanation: $f=c/\lambda=3\times10^8/300=1\times10^6$ Hz $=1$ MHz.

questions.q: Satellite communication (uplink/downlink) uses microwaves rather than ordinary long-wavelength radio waves mainly because microwaves
options: can penetrate the ionosphere without being reflected back
questions.explanation: Lower-frequency radio waves are reflected by the ionosphere, but microwaves are short enough in wavelength to pass through it, making them suitable for communicating with satellites.

questions.q: Television signals (very high frequency) are transmitted using tall antennas because they propagate mainly as
options: waves that travel through the earth's core
space waves, requiring line-of-sight transmission since they are not reflected by the ionosphere
ground waves that follow the earth's curvature over long distances
sky waves reflected multiple times by the ionosphere
questions.explanation: VHF/UHF television signals are neither reflected by the ionosphere nor diffract appreciably around the earth's curvature, so they travel as space (line-of-sight) waves, requiring tall transmitting/receiving antennas.

questions.q: Night-vision (thermal imaging) cameras can form images in complete darkness because they detect
options: gamma radiation emitted by warm bodies
ultraviolet radiation absorbed by the lens
infrared radiation emitted by all objects due to their temperature
questions.explanation: All objects above absolute zero continuously emit infrared (thermal) radiation; thermal cameras detect this IR emission to form an image even without any visible light.

questions.q: Which statement about ultraviolet radiation is correct?
options: It cannot be absorbed by the ozone layer
It has a longer wavelength than visible light
It helps in the production of vitamin D in the skin but excessive exposure can cause skin cancer and damage the eyes
It is completely harmless in any amount
questions.explanation: UV radiation triggers vitamin D synthesis in skin in small doses, but prolonged exposure causes skin cancer and eye damage; most harmful UV is absorbed by the ozone layer.

questions.q: X-rays are used to study crystal structures (X-ray diffraction) because
options: they travel slower than visible light in crystals
their wavelength is comparable to the interatomic spacing in crystals
questions.explanation: Diffraction effects are prominent when wavelength is comparable to the spacing of scattering centres; X-ray wavelengths (~0.1 nm) match typical interatomic distances in crystals.

questions.q: In medicine, gamma rays are used for
options: stimulating vitamin D synthesis in skin
cancer radiotherapy and sterilising surgical equipment
producing images using visible light contrast
questions.explanation: The high energy and penetrating power of gamma rays make them useful for destroying cancerous cells (radiotherapy) and sterilising medical instruments.

questions.q: Displacement current was introduced by Maxwell as a modification to
questions.explanation: Maxwell added the displacement current term $\varepsilon_0d\Phi_E/dt$ to Ampere's law, giving $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=\mu_0(I_c+I_d)$, making it consistent with charge conservation.

questions.q: While a parallel plate capacitor is being charged, inside the gap between the plates there is
options: an electric current due to free electrons crossing the gap
a conduction current equal to that in the wires, and no displacement current
no conduction current but a displacement current equal to the conduction current in the connecting wires
questions.explanation: No charge crosses the gap (no conduction current), but the changing electric flux between the plates produces a displacement current numerically equal to the conduction current in the wires, keeping the circuit current continuous.

questions.q: A microwave oven heats food by
options: directly burning the food surface with infrared radiation
causing water molecules in the food to rotate/vibrate rapidly, converting microwave energy to heat (dielectric heating)
using ultraviolet radiation to sterilise the food
passing an electric current through the food
questions.explanation: Microwaves at a frequency matched to water's rotational absorption cause water molecules in the food to oscillate rapidly, generating heat throughout the food (dielectric heating).

questions.q: Visible light of wavelength 600 nm has a frequency of
questions.explanation: $f=c/\lambda=3\times10^8/(600\times10^{-9})=5\times10^{14}$ Hz.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave is described by $E = E_0\sin(kx-\omega t)$ with $k=2\times10^7$ rad/m and $\omega=6\times10^{15}$ rad/s. Its speed is
questions.explanation: Wave speed $v=\omega/k=(6\times10^{15})/(2\times10^7)=3\times10^8$ m/s, as expected for an EM wave in vacuum.

questions.q: The existence of electromagnetic waves, predicted theoretically by Maxwell, was first experimentally demonstrated by
questions.explanation: Heinrich Hertz generated and detected radio waves in the laboratory in 1887, confirming Maxwell's theoretical prediction of electromagnetic waves.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists electromagnetic radiations in order of increasing wavelength?
options: IR, visible, UV, radio, microwave, X-rays, gamma
Gamma rays, X-rays, UV, visible, IR, microwave, radio
Radio, microwave, IR, visible, UV, X-rays, gamma rays
Visible, IR, UV, X-rays, radio, microwave, gamma
questions.explanation: Wavelength increases as frequency decreases, so the order is gamma rays < X-rays < UV < visible < IR < microwave < radio — exactly the reverse of the increasing-frequency order.

questions.q: The refractive indices of two transparent media for a given electromagnetic (light) wave are 1.5 and 2.0. The ratio of speeds of the wave in the two media ($v_1:v_2$) is
Sunlight of intensity 1000 W/m$^2$ falls normally on a perfectly absorbing surface of area 2 m$^2$. The force exerted by radiation on the surface is approximately
questions.explanation: Radiation pressure for total absorption $p=I/c=1000/(3\times10^8)\approx3.3\times10^{-6}$ Pa; force $=p\times A\approx3.3\times10^{-6}\times2\approx6.7\times10^{-6}$ N.
